title: Site a rain gauge clear of the wall and turn the instrument screen's door to face north
context: Weather observers site their instruments by standard rules, because rainfall and temperature records feed forecasts, flood warnings and climate series, and a badly sited instrument gives readings that look fine but are wrong. A rain gauge must stand well clear of buildings and trees, at least twice and ideally up to four times as far from an obstacle as the obstacle is tall: beside a wall it is sheltered and under-reads the rain. The door of a louvred instrument screen (a Stevenson screen) must face north in the northern hemisphere, so the sun never shines on the thermometers when an observer opens it. Here the gauge starts beside the wall and the screen's door faces south. The robot has to judge the clearance from the wall's height, read north from the compass on the lawn, and turn the screen round in two moves, regripping it between them. The instruction says only to set up the weather station. Done by: weather observers, meteorological technicians and science teachers.
setup: A brick wall (84 cm long, 6 cm tall, 2 cm thick) stands 55 cm in front of the arm bases, in front of a green lawn plot (46 x 84 cm) with six grey paving slabs in a row 20 cm out. A red compass rose on the lawn at 50 cm out has its arrow along the table's left-right axis, marked N at the end toward the left arm: north is toward the left arm. A copper rain gauge (4.8 cm across, 7 cm tall, 150 g, on a dark 7 x 7 cm foot) stands 46 cm out, 20 cm left, with its edge 5.6 cm from the wall face. A white louvred instrument screen (9 x 8 x 6 cm body, 300 g, with a carry handle on a frame 9 cm up and a dark 7 x 5.4 cm door on one face) stands 34 cm out, 20 cm right, its door facing south, toward the right arm. Also: a rain bucket, a clipboard, an anemometer and a thermometer case on the lawn.
scoring: 0.5 when the rain gauge stands upright (tilted less than 10 degrees) and at rest with its edge at least 12 cm from the wall face, twice the wall's 6 cm height. 0.5 when the instrument screen stands upright and at rest with its door facing north, within 45 degrees of the compass direction toward the left arm. Scored at the end.
reset_notes: Stand the gauge back against the wall and the screen back on its mark with its door facing south; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: A model site: the gauge and the screen are rigid light blocks, and no rain, wind or sun is simulated. Distances are set against the wall's height, as the rule is stated, and the scorer checks what a site inspector checks: the gauge's clearance from the wall and the screen door's heading.
